speaker_role: test-prep/consultancy marketer ('Crazy Medusa' channel, promotes a research bootcamp product)
commercial_incentive: Yes - directly promotes a paid 8-week research bootcamp ('Incognito Blueprint') multiple times, plus references personally advising students
key_insights: Speaker frames the video around AI making essays/reports easy to fake, arguing applicants must show verifiable 'proof' (credentials, external validation) rather than just descriptive claims
Recommends validating research projects through poster presentations, science competitions, or publication rather than just writing an unreviewed paper

For hackathons/incubators/startups, recommends showing sustained escalating commitment (e.g. progressing from short to 24-hour hackathons) and measurable impact rather than one-off participation certificates

Argues startup involvement doesn't require being the founder or making money; community-impact projects (two small examples given: local pothole-repair initiative, pet memoir-writing service) can be compelling if genuine and small-scale
Warns admissions officers can search claims online, so all activities described should have some discoverable/verifiable online presence to avoid looking fabricated

Recommends building a verifiable portfolio: Google Scholar/ResearchGate for publications, GitHub for CS contributions, or an online portfolio tool, since these are hard to fake and support application claims
Suggests participating in a target college's own pre-admission programs (e.g. named example: Yale Young Global Scholars) as a way to build a relationship with that school before applying
specific_numbers_or_facts: Named example graduate-level competitions: MIT 100K, Rice Business Plan Competition, Stanford BASES
Named example pre-college program: Yale Young Global Scholars Program
Research bootcamp described as 8 weeks long, open to students from grade 9 onward
notable_or_distinctive: Frames advice explicitly around the AI era, arguing verifiability/proof of authenticity (competitions, publications, GitHub, Google Scholar) is now more important than descriptive claims since AI can fabricate polished-sounding work.
reliability_notes: Heavily promotional for the speaker's own paid research program; specific claims about what 'impresses' officers are asserted without citation, and anecdotes (pothole startup, pet memoir startup) are unverifiable individual examples presented as generalizable strategy.
